disease_label_per_paper: Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia with septic shock, pneumonia, sepsis-induced agranulocytosis, and gingival necrosis
presentation_summary: Previously healthy 29-year-old woman presented with burning gingival pain, progressive purple-white necrotic gingival lesions, malaise, odynophagia, abdominal pain, intermittent nausea and vomiting, and febrile tachycardia.
Initial examination showed bilateral submandibular lymphadenopathy and necrosis of attached gingiva across upper anterior teeth and other gingival margins.
Initial full blood count showed severe leukopenia with WBC 0.19 x10^9/L and normal platelets; she then decompensated with BP 64/45 mmHg and heart rate 148/min.
Chest imaging showed lower-lobe air-space consolidation; blood cultures later reported pansensitive Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia.

risk_context.source_text_value: symptoms started roughly a month before presentation since her return from a developing country
severe leukopenia with 0.19 x 10^9/L; individual leukocyte subtypes were so low that they could not be quantified
The patient reported no known medical conditions
Augmentin 625 mg twice a day was prescribed before presentation

observations.source_text_value: intermittent fever and febrile at triage
mixed purple and white necrotic lesions with sloughing around gingival margins
necrosis of the buccal attached gingiva of the upper anterior region extending up the frenum
air-space consolidation in the lower lobes of the lungs
febrile tachycardia, severe leukopenia, pneumonia imaging, and shock physiology
necrotizing oral lesions, severe leukopenia/agranulocytosis, lower-lobe pneumonia, and septic shock
entered a state of shock with marked hypotension and tachycardia

imaging.source_text_value: Initial clinical presentation of necrotic buccal attached gingiva; mixed purple and white necrotic lesions with sloughing
Erect chest radiography and computed tomography showed air-space consolidation in the lower lobes of the lungs, suggestive of pneumonia
Radiographic examination revealed normal bone levels and no obvious pathology

microbiology.source_text_value: blood cultures reported pansensitive Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteraemia
her human immunodeficiency virus screen was negative

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: gingival necrosis was attributed to sepsis-induced agranulocytosis triggered by Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteraemia
diagnosis of community-acquired Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia that led to sepsis and septic shock

actual_treatment.source_text_value: empirically started on intravenous piperacillin/tazobactam and vancomycin
Vancomycin administration was paused, and the patient improved clinically
discharged after a week and prescribed another week of oral ciprofloxacin

outcome.source_text_value: secondary healing over exposed alveolar bone was noted after a year-long follow-up, with residual gingival recession

quality_warnings: Gingival necrosis and pneumonia are presentation/source axes, not disease-name qualifiers.
Pseudomonas species and pansusceptibility are kept as non-ranking confirmatory evidence.
